issues.title: [epic] S1: run scanners in a sandbox
issues.body:
## Context

Scanners parse hostile layers and currently run unsandboxed as the invoking user (THREAT_MODEL.md, residual risks). Uncompressed layer size is bounded only by the scanner and disk.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Scanners run with read-only root FS, tmpfs with quota, no network except vulnerability DB mirrors, seccomp profile
- [ ] Sandbox backend pluggable (bubblewrap on Linux hosts, rootless OCI runtime in containers)
- [ ] Hostile fixture suite (see linked issue) passes with every case bounded and reported as a health finding
- [ ] ADR documenting the chosen backends and residual risk

## References

THREAT_MODEL.md · ADR 0006

issues.title: [epic] F12: native registry providers (RegistryProvider extension point)
issues.body:
## Context

M1 authenticates through docker config and credential helpers only. F12 requires native providers with short-lived credentials and repository listing. This epic introduces the `RegistryProvider` interface + registry and the conformance checks for it.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `RegistryProvider` interface (keychain + repository/tag listing) with plugin registry, mirrored on scanner plugins
- [ ] Conformance kit for providers (auth failure classification, redaction, pagination limits)
- [ ] ECR and GitLab providers implemented (linked issues)
- [ ] docs/extending/registry-provider.md

## References

SPEC.md F12 · docs/extending/README.md

issues.title: [epic] F5: OpenVEX and CycloneDX VEX import/export
issues.body:
## Context

Decisions (risk_accepted, not_affected) are stored append-only but cannot yet be exchanged as VEX. VEX is how vendors and downstream consumers express not_affected with justification.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `shieldmon vex import` maps OpenVEX/CycloneDX VEX statements to decisions (scoped by product digest/PURL/vuln)
- [ ] `shieldmon vex export` emits valid OpenVEX for current decisions, validated against the spec schema
- [ ] Imported statements require author and justification; expiry honoured; unknown products reported, not dropped
- [ ] Round-trip test import → export → import is lossless

## References

SPEC.md F5 · ADR 0004

issues.title: [epic] F9: notifications (Notifier extension point)
issues.body:
## Context

Nothing is pushed to humans yet: SLA breaches, new KEV findings and health findings are only visible via CLI/report.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `Notifier` interface + registry; events: new critical/KEV finding, SLA breach upcoming/breached, health finding opened
- [ ] Deduplication (same event never sent twice) and digest mode (one summary per cycle)
- [ ] Webhook and SMTP notifiers built in; others as adapters (linked issues)
- [ ] Secrets for notifiers never logged; redaction tests

## References

SPEC.md F9

issues.title: [epic] F11: Helm chart ingestion and neglected-chart tracking
issues.body:
## Context

Many Helm charts ship stale images. ShieldMon should ingest charts, extract every image, track chart versions and help upstream fix them. OCI Helm charts are currently rejected safely as non-images.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `ChartSource` interface: HTTP repos, OCI registries, Artifact Hub
- [ ] Render with defaults + values profiles; extract images from containers, initContainers, ephemeral containers and hook Jobs
- [ ] Flag images rendering cannot reveal (operator/CRD-managed)
- [ ] Track per chart version; detect neglected charts (fix available upstream, not adopted)
- [ ] Upstream contribution queue (linked issue)

## References

SPEC.md F11

issues.title: Detect stale or end-of-life base image lineages
issues.body:
## Context

Found in the UBI 9 + Node.js e2e scenario: rebuilding on the latest `ubi9/nodejs-20-minimal` (Node 20 EOL, last rebuilt 2026-05-12) left ~250 OS/npm findings that already had an upstream fix, while `nodejs-22-minimal` was rebuilt on 2026-10-13. Rebuilding cannot remediate anything when the base lineage is no longer maintained.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Identify the base image of a target (OCI base annotations, history, or configured mapping)
- [ ] Health/finding when the newest tag of the base lineage is older than N days, or when the image has many findings fixable by the newest base
- [ ] Report section "fixable by rebuild" vs "needs base migration"
- [ ] Suggest the maintained successor lineage when known (e.g. nodejs-20 → nodejs-22)

issues.title: Keep the UBI 9 + Node.js e2e scenario green and representative

## Context

`examples/ubi9-node/e2e.py` (CI job `e2e-ubi9-node`) is the end-to-end quality gate: multi-stage build, OS+npm findings, remediation decision policy, rebuild, base migration, reports. Base tags and npm pins are fixed in the script and age over time.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Renovate (or a scheduled job) proposes bumps of the pinned base tags
- [ ] Assertions stay independent of the exact number of CVEs in the vulnerability DB
- [ ] Reports from the job are linked from the README as a live example

issues.title: Seccomp filter for sandboxed scanners
issues.body:
## Context

ADR 0011, decision 5: one deny-list seccomp filter shared by every sandbox backend, generated in pure Go (the binary is built with `CGO_ENABLED=0`). The `bwrap` backend runs scanners without one today, so a compromised parser can still create user namespaces, use io_uring or bpf, and reach the kernel attack surface they expose.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Filter generated in Go for amd64 and arm64 with `golang.org/x/sys/unix` (no new module); any other architecture, and the i386 and x32 ABIs, are refused
- [ ] Denies namespace creation (`unshare`, `setns`, `clone` with `CLONE_NEW*`, `clone3`), `ptrace` and `process_vm_*`, the mount family, keyrings, `bpf`, `perf_event_open`, `userfaultfd`, io_uring, kernel modules, `kexec`, and `personality` changes
- [ ] `bwrap` loads it with `--seccomp`; the `landlock` launcher applies the same filter
- [ ] Unit tests evaluate the BPF program; `scannertest.CheckSandbox` proves a confined process cannot create a user namespace

issues.title: Landlock sandbox backend for containers (`shieldmon sandbox-exec`)
issues.body:
## Context

ADR 0011, decision 4: container runtimes deny `unshare(CLONE_NEWUSER)` by default, so `bwrap` cannot start in a Kubernetes CronJob (#7, #11). Landlock is unprivileged, needs no namespace and is inherited across `execve`. It replaces the rootless OCI runtime named in the epic, which needs the same user namespaces.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Hidden `shieldmon sandbox-exec` launcher applies Landlock filesystem rules from the policy, denies TCP connect/bind when offline (Landlock ABI ≥ 4, otherwise it refuses), sets `RLIMIT_FSIZE`/`RLIMIT_NOFILE`, `no_new_privs` and the seccomp filter, then execs the scanner
- [ ] Registered as `landlock`, tried by `auto` after `bwrap`; availability reports the kernel's Landlock ABI
- [ ] Passes `scannertest.CheckSandbox` in CI (`SHIELDMON_TEST_SANDBOX=landlock`)
- [ ] Implemented with `golang.org/x/sys/unix` (no new module)

issues.title: Disk quota for sandboxed scanners' scratch space
issues.body:
## Context

Scratch space is a per-process directory under `<data_dir>/tmp` on disk: a RAM-backed tmpfs big enough for real images would let a decompression bomb exhaust host memory (ADR 0011, implementation notes). A hostile layer can therefore still fill the data dir's disk.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Each scanner process's writes are bounded: single files (`RLIMIT_FSIZE`) and the scratch directory in total
- [ ] Exceeding the quota stops the scanner and fails the scan with a health finding, without filling the disk
- [ ] `scannertest.CheckSandbox` probes the quota

issues.title: Sandbox scanners by default (`scanners.sandbox.backend: auto`)
issues.body:
## Context

ADR 0011, decision 4: the default `auto` picks `bwrap`, then `landlock`, and refuses to scan when neither runs. The default stays `none` until the Landlock backend lands, so that ShieldMon still scans in containers.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Built-in default and `shieldmon init` template use `auto`
- [ ] Getting started and deployment docs cover hosts without a backend (macOS development: explicit `backend: none`)
- [ ] Configs that set `backend` explicitly keep their value; the release notes say what changes for configs that do not

issues.title: AppArmor: evaluate the upstream bwrap-userns-restrict profile for hosts
issues.body:
## Context

`deploy/apparmor/shieldmon-bwrap` grants `userns` to `/usr/bin/bwrap` unconfined. On a shared Ubuntu host every local user can then use bwrap to regain the kernel attack surface that `kernel.apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_userns` removes (ADR 0011, implementation notes). AppArmor's `bwrap-userns-restrict` profile lets bwrap set up its namespaces while the processes it starts run without capabilities.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Tried on `ubuntu-24.04` with ShieldMon's bwrap arguments: `scannertest.CheckSandbox` passes
- [ ] If it works, `deploy/apparmor` and ADR 0011 recommend it for hosts; CI may keep the simple profile
- [ ] If it does not, ADR 0011 records why

issues.title: One confinement path for both sandbox backends: W^X, file size limit under bwrap, quota in the kit
issues.body:
## Context

Review of #47 found three gaps: writable directories are executable under both backends (Landlock grants EXECUTE on them, bwrap's bind mounts are not noexec), `RLIMIT_FSIZE` is set only under `landlock`, and `scannertest.CheckSandbox` does not probe the scratch quota. Seccomp is applied by two code paths (bwrap `--seccomp`, the Landlock launcher).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `bwrap` runs the scanner through `shieldmon sandbox-exec` inside its namespaces: `no_new_privs`, rlimits (`RLIMIT_FSIZE` included), Landlock when the kernel has it, and seccomp come from one launcher for both backends
- [ ] W^X: no process can execute a file in a directory it can write (Landlock rights)
- [ ] `bwrap` on a kernel without Landlock keeps working and keeps a `scanner_sandbox_degraded` health finding open; `doctor` warns
- [ ] `scannertest.CheckSandbox` probes W^X, the scratch quota and the file size limit through a Runner

issues.title: Dedicated scratch filesystem: deployment examples and doctor check
issues.body:
## Context

The scratch quota is enforced by the Runner's watch, which can overshoot by 100 ms of writing (ADR 0011, #47). A kernel-enforced total needs a size-limited filesystem, which only the deployment can create. Mounted `noexec,nosuid,nodev` at `<data_dir>/tmp`, it also gives W^X to every scanner output at mount level, including under `bwrap` on kernels without Landlock (#53).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Examples for a host (loop image or LV, mount unit) and Kubernetes (generic ephemeral volume) in `deploy/scratch`
- [ ] `shieldmon doctor` reports whether `<data_dir>/tmp` is a dedicated filesystem, its size against `limits.max_scratch_bytes`, and missing `noexec`/`nosuid`/`nodev`; warnings, not failures
- [ ] Not required: without it, the watch and the free-disk floor stay the default protection

issues.title: RegistryProvider extension point: interface, registry, conformance kit, built-in providers
issues.body:
## Context

Credentials come from one hard-wired keychain (docker config, then ECR, then Google) and nothing can list repositories or tags. Epic #2 asks for a `RegistryProvider` extension point mirrored on scanner plugins, a conformance kit, and docs.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `oci.Provider` (keychain + bounded repository and tag listing) with `oci.RegisterProvider`; `shieldmon plugins` lists providers
- [ ] Today's sources become built-in providers (`docker`, `ecr`, `google`) applied in the same order, so nothing changes for existing setups
- [ ] `registries:` config binds hosts to providers with validated options; credentials only through environment variables, never literal values
- [ ] Listing is bounded (pages, bytes, entries) and validates every name a registry returns
- [ ] `ocitest.CheckProvider`: owned vs foreign hosts, limits, cancellation, 401/403 classified as auth failures, secrets absent from errors
- [ ] ADR and docs/extending/registry-provider.md

issues.title: VEX import: OpenVEX and CycloneDX VEX statements as scoped not_affected decisions
issues.body:
## Context

Decisions are recorded per finding by hand. A VEX statement (from a vendor, or another team) says a vulnerability does not affect a product, and must keep applying to findings detected later.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `shieldmon vex import FILE` parses OpenVEX and CycloneDX VEX (bounded, hostile input, fuzzed)
- [ ] Statements are stored append-only, scoped by product (image digest or repository), optional package PURL (with or without version) and vulnerability (with aliases)
- [ ] Imported statements need an author and a justification; past expiry is refused, a future one is honoured
- [ ] They apply now to matching findings and, through the engine, to findings found later; statements for products not seen yet are kept and reported, not dropped
- [ ] ADR

issues.title: VEX export: OpenVEX from statements and not_affected decisions, schema-validated
issues.body:
## Context

Downstream consumers and auditors need ShieldMon's not_affected decisions as standard VEX.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `shieldmon vex export` emits OpenVEX 0.2.0 for the statements in force and the not_affected decisions taken by hand
- [ ] Validated against the OpenVEX JSON schema in tests
- [ ] Round trip import → export → import is lossless

issues.title: Notifier extension point: events, deduplication, digest mode, conformance kit
issues.body:
## Context

Epic #4 needs the `Notifier` interface, the events, deduplication and digest mode before the adapters (#23, #24, #25).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `notify.Notifier` + `notify.RegisterNotifier`; `shieldmon plugins` lists notifiers; `notifytest.CheckNotifier`
- [ ] Events after each monitor cycle: new critical finding, new KEV finding, SLA due soon, SLA breached, health finding opened
- [ ] An event is sent at most once per channel (append-only record); digest mode sends one message per cycle
- [ ] A failing channel opens a `notify_failed` health finding; secrets only from environment variables, never in errors or logs
- [ ] `shieldmon notify preview` and `shieldmon notify test CHANNEL`; ADR

issues.title: Store compares RFC 3339 timestamps as text in SQL: decision expiry can slip a cycle
issues.body:
## Context

`store.ExpireDecisions` (`internal/store/lifecycle.go`) selects expired decisions with `d.expires_at <= ?`, comparing `ts()` strings in SQL. `ts` formats with `time.RFC3339Nano`, which drops trailing zeros, so the strings do not sort as times within the same second: `2026-10-11T09:00:00Z` sorts after `2026-10-11T09:00:00.5Z` ('Z' > '.').

Effect: a decision expiring in the same second as the cycle's clock is not seen as expired and is reopened one cycle later. Low impact, but it understates the time a finding was suppressed after expiry, and the same pattern may exist elsewhere.

Found while writing the notification store (#66), which compares times in Go for this reason.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Reproduce with a store test (expiry and now in the same second, fractional seconds)
- [ ] Fix: compare in Go, or store a fixed-width format (e.g. always 9 fractional digits) via a new numbered migration that rewrites nothing in append-only tables
- [ ] Audit every SQL comparison or ORDER BY on `*_at` columns (store, report)

issues.title: [epic] Inventory: what is monitored, what it contains, how fresh the evidence is
issues.body:
## Context

Epic #5 (F8) asks for an inventory export next to the remediation plan. Auditors and incident
responders ask three questions before they look at findings:

1. **What is monitored?** Every image, the digest it runs, since when, and whether ShieldMon
   still has fresh evidence for it.
2. **What does it contain?** Which components (packages, versions, PURLs) are in which images:
   "are we running xz 5.6.0 anywhere?" must be answerable in seconds, from SBOMs already stored.
3. **What changed?** Images added, rebuilt (new digests) and retired during a period.

ShieldMon already records most of this (targets, the append-only digest history, SBOMs with
SHA-256, scans with tools and DB build times) but only shows it piecemeal (`targets list`,
`sbom list`). Targets cannot be retired at all: a decommissioned image stays "monitored"
forever, which makes both the inventory and the open-finding numbers wrong.

## Goals

- One command for the image inventory, one for components, both exportable (CSV, JSON) and
  reproducible from the store like the monthly report.
- Evidence gaps visible: images without a recent complete scan, without an SBOM from a
  required generator, or scanned unconfined.
- Asset lifecycle: retire a target without rewriting history.

## Non-goals

- Runtime inventory (which images actually run in a cluster): that is the runtime context work
  of #38.
- License compliance: licenses are carried when SBOMs have them, not evaluated.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] #69 Image inventory report
- [ ] #70 Component inventory and "where is this package" query from stored SBOMs
- [ ] #71 Inventory changes over a period
- [ ] #72 Target retirement with an ADR: history kept, retired images out of the open numbers
- [ ] #73 Aggregated CycloneDX inventory BOM
- [ ] docs/processes/inventory.md; SPEC F8 updated

## Risks

- SBOMs are hostile input: component parsing must be bounded and fuzzed like every parser.
- Retirement touches the lifecycle invariants (only `lifecycle.Reconcile` closes findings):
  it needs an ADR before code.

## References

SPEC.md F8 · Epic #5 · docs/processes/reporting.md

issues.title: Image inventory: `shieldmon report inventory` with digests, SBOMs and scan evidence
issues.body:
## Context

The first inventory question: what is monitored, and how fresh is the evidence for it.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `shieldmon report inventory -o csv|json|md [--out FILE]`: one row per target with ref, platform,
  current digest, repository, monitored since, last resolved, digest changes so far, last scan
  (time, kind, status, scanners with versions and DB build times), SBOMs (generator, format,
  SHA-256, size) and open findings by severity
- [ ] Evidence gaps per row and in a summary: no scan yet, last scan partial or failed, last
  complete scan older than `health.monitor_interval` x 1.5, a required generator without SBOM
- [ ] Deterministic order; formula-injection safe CSV; golden-file tests
- [ ] Files written 0600 (an inventory is sensitive); docs/processes/inventory.md

issues.title: Component inventory: packages per image from stored SBOMs, and `components where`
issues.body:
## Context

During an incident the question is "where do we run package X (version Y)?". Every monitored
digest has CycloneDX SBOMs on disk; nothing reads them back except the matchers.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Parse stored CycloneDX SBOMs into components (name, version, type, PURL, licenses when
  present): bounded (size, count, depth), SHA-256 checked against the store before parsing,
  fuzzed (`make fuzz`)
- [ ] `shieldmon components list [--target T] [-o csv|json]`: components of the current digests,
  deduplicated by PURL, with the images that contain them
- [ ] `shieldmon components where NAME[@VERSION]|PURL`: images (targets and digests) containing
  it, exact or by package name; exit code 1 when none, for scripts
- [ ] Hostile names escaped on terminal output; formula-safe CSV; tests with trimmed real SBOMs

issues.title: Inventory changes over a period: images added, rebuilt and retired
issues.body:
## Context

Auditors compare inventories between periods. The append-only `target_digests` history already
says when each image was added and rebuilt.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `shieldmon report inventory --month YYYY-MM` adds the changes of the month: targets added,
  digest changes (old → new, with the scan that proved the new one), targets retired
- [ ] The monthly report gains an "Inventory changes" section (md, html, json)
- [ ] Computed from the append-only history only: reproducible for any past month

issues.title: Retire targets: stop monitoring a decommissioned image, keep its history
issues.body:
## Context

There is no way to stop monitoring an image: decommissioned images keep their open findings
in every report and keep being resolved every cycle.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] ADR first: retirement is an asset event, not a fix. Findings of a retired target are not
  closed as `fixed` (no scan evidence); decide how they leave the open numbers (e.g. reported
  as "retired with the asset") without breaking invariants I1-I7
- [ ] `shieldmon targets retire TARGET --reason ... --by ...` and `targets restore`; recorded
  append-only with actor and reason; `monitor` skips retired targets
- [ ] Inventory and monthly reports show retired targets and exclude their findings from open
  counts as decided in the ADR; step in `TestContinuousMonitoringLifecycle`

issues.title: Aggregated CycloneDX inventory BOM of all monitored images
issues.body:
## Context

Customers and regulators increasingly ask for an SBOM of the whole product, not one per image.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `shieldmon report inventory -o cyclonedx`: one CycloneDX 1.6 BOM with each monitored image as
  a container component (digest as hash, repository and tag as PURL) and its components nested
- [ ] Valid against the CycloneDX 1.6 JSON schema (pinned in testdata); bounded size
